baseline_facts: Abdomen: Mild epigastric tenderness without guarding. Rectal examination reveals black tarry stool.
Bedside ultrasound, left ventricle: Small cavity with hyperdynamic contraction; near-obliteration of the cavity in systole
Bedside ultrasound, inferior vena cava: 0.9 cm; near-complete inspiratory collapse
items.context: A 57-year-old man presents after nearly fainting when standing. He looks pale and says he feels profoundly weak. Authored diagnosis: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding with hemorrhagic hypoperfusion.
items.intervention: Norepinephrine 10 mcg/min, started at minute 2 and kept at that rate to the end. Nothing else is given or changed; the underlying problem is left untreated.
items.note: An authored synthetic case for development, not a patient.
items.purpose: Does norepinephrine produce a pressure response with an appropriate direction, timing, and magnitude in this patient with ongoing hemorrhage, without implying that vasopressor support corrects the underlying volume loss?

timeline.result: Infusion kept at 10 mcg/min to minute 32 (no titration, no stop)

items.title: 57-year-old man with an upper gastrointestinal bleed: norepinephrine during ongoing hemorrhage

baseline_facts: The heart and the circulating volume are not changed during the probe.
There is no patient, no history and no examination: this is a physiology probe.
items.context: A synthetic state, not a patient: vascular tone falls over the first 4 minutes (a scripted loss of tone) while the heart and the circulating volume are unchanged. The pressure before the fall is 120/75 mmHg (MAP 90).
items.intervention: Norepinephrine 10 mcg/min, started at minute 10 and kept at that rate to the end. Nothing else is given or changed.
items.note: This is a synthetic development physiology probe, not a clinical case.
items.purpose: Does vascular-tone support move pressure toward a more plausible state without creating flow or volume?

timeline.result: Infusion kept at 10 mcg/min to minute 40 (no titration, no stop)

items.title: SYNTHETIC DEVELOPMENT PHYSIOLOGY PROBE: loss of vascular tone, then norepinephrine

baseline_facts: Respiratory: Mildly increased effort; scattered basal crackles.
Bedside ultrasound, left ventricle: Globally mildly reduced contraction without a single focal defect
Bedside ultrasound, inferior vena cava: 1.9 cm; about 50% inspiratory collapse
Bedside ultrasound, lungs: Scattered B-lines at both bases; no diffuse B-line pattern
items.context: A 70-year-old woman presents with chest pressure, breathlessness and sweating that began an hour ago. Authored diagnosis: Left main or severe three-vessel ischemia with diffuse ST depression and ST elevation in aVR.
items.intervention: Norepinephrine 10 mcg/min, started at minute 5 and kept at that rate to the end. Nothing else is given or changed; the underlying problem is left untreated.
items.note: An authored synthetic case for development, not a patient.
items.purpose: Does the pressure response to norepinephrine remain clinically defensible in a patient whose forward flow is limited, without implying that vasoconstriction corrects pump failure?

timeline.result: Infusion kept at 10 mcg/min to minute 30 (no titration, no stop)

items.title: 70-year-old woman with a left main acute coronary syndrome: norepinephrine with limited forward flow

baseline_facts: Respiratory: Severe respiratory effort with widespread bilateral crackles and some expiratory wheeze.
Bedside ultrasound, left ventricle: Moderately reduced global contraction
Bedside ultrasound, inferior vena cava: 2.4 cm; <50% inspiratory collapse
Bedside ultrasound, lungs: Diffuse bilateral B-lines in the anterior and lateral zones
items.context: A 58-year-old man arrives with rapidly worsening breathlessness. He remains upright and can speak only a few words at a time. Authored diagnosis: Hypertensive acute cardiogenic pulmonary edema.
items.intervention: Norepinephrine 10 mcg/min, started at minute 5 and kept at that rate to the end. Nothing else is given or changed; the underlying problem is left untreated.
items.note: An authored synthetic case for development, not a patient.
items.purpose: Does norepinephrine produce a pressure response that is directionally plausible without overstating benefit in a congested, pump-limited patient?

timeline.result: Infusion kept at 10 mcg/min to minute 30 (no titration, no stop)

items.title: 58-year-old man with hypertensive pulmonary edema: norepinephrine in a congested, pump-limited patient

baseline_facts: Bedside ultrasound, right ventricle: Larger than the LV; septal flattening with a D-shaped LV; reduced free-wall contraction with apical sparing (McConnell sign)
Bedside ultrasound, left ventricle: Small, underfilled cavity with vigorous contraction
Bedside ultrasound, inferior vena cava: 2.3 cm; minimal inspiratory collapse
Extremities: Left calf swelling and tenderness.
items.context: A 61-year-old man is brought in after nearly collapsing. He is breathless and says he feels faint even while lying on the trolley. Authored diagnosis: High-risk pulmonary embolism with obstructive shock.
items.intervention: Norepinephrine 10 mcg/min, started at minute 5 and kept at that rate to the end. Nothing else is given or changed; the underlying problem is left untreated.
items.note: An authored synthetic case for development, not a patient.
items.purpose: Does norepinephrine produce a plausible pressure response in an obstructive low-flow state without implying correction of the underlying obstruction?

timeline.result: Infusion kept at 10 mcg/min to minute 30 (no titration, no stop)

items.title: 61-year-old man with a high-risk pulmonary embolism: norepinephrine in an obstructive low-flow state

limitations.text: How strongly the pressure response depends on the state of the pump is not yet validated. The ACS and pulmonary-edema judgments inform whether the pathway is acceptable for development; they do not support educational promotion.
Consciousness under vascular-tone support was neither shown nor judged in this review. It remains unresolved.
Only a single start of norepinephrine at a fixed rate is represented. Titration, rate changes and stopping the infusion are not supported.

statement: Synthetic development cases and one synthetic physiology probe. A faculty judgment of stored development trajectories of ONE norepinephrine order: not a clinical validation, not a calibrated configuration, not a score, not a resident pilot.
what_it_is: Five review scenarios of ONE norepinephrine order (a start at 10 mcg/min, never changed) -- a hemorrhage, a synthetic low-tone probe, a pump-limited ACS, a congested pulmonary edema and an obstructive pulmonary embolism -- with the trajectories of the CENTER_REFERENCE setting taken from, or proven equal to, the certified common-tone records. No comparator, no earlier trajectory and no other set are part of the items.
